EO 14404 (signed 2026-05-01; 91 FR 25061; official Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_14404.txt, read in full) imposes blocking sanctions on persons responsible for repression in Cuba and threats to United States national security, suspends their entry, authorizes sanctions on foreign financial institutions, delegates implementation and sets reporting and general provisions, acting under the national emergency declared in Executive Order 14380. Identity: the Title 3 heading of Executive Order 14404 of May 1, 2026, imposing sanctions on those responsible for repression in Cuba at 91 FR 25061, the title and the date agree with the register row. The dossier inventory has thirty-one clauses covering sections 1 to 8 (with the criteria of section 2(a)(i) in one clause and section 2(c)(i) to (iii) in three); I confirmed it without correction, noting that it omits the unnumbered authority recital, which orders nothing, and that its scope identifiers sec2-i-dup2 and sec2-i-ii, sec2-i-iii are section 2(c)(i), (ii) and (iii) and sec4-i, sec4-i-ii and sec8-i, sec8-i-ii are paragraphs (i) and (ii) of the sections named. Own terms: no section has an end date or ending condition; the national emergency on which it rests was declared on 2026-01-29 and a continuation notice was not due before 2026-10-14. Later instruments: a search of every held order text for the number 14404 finds only the order's own Federal Register copy, the Federal Register contents page of May 7, 2026, the held 31 CFR part 516 and Federal Register notices of designations under it; EO 14389 of February 20, 2026 ends additional ad valorem duties under EO 14380 and other orders but states that the Cuba national emergency remains in effect and does not name this order. The dossier chain has no event. No held text revokes, supersedes or amends it. The three selected machine searches (current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog) were read with their coverage notes, carry no coverage warning, and record 5, 5 and 1 hits for the order number respectively. Limit stated plainly: the continuing predicate rests on the held original text and the bounded searches (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09); the text of EO 14380 is held in the repository but not as packet evidence and the National Emergencies Act and IEEPA texts are not held, so the emergency's continuation rests on the order's own recital, the date arithmetic of the Act's anniversary rule and EO 14389's statement that it remains in effect, and the held evidence does not show whether any joint resolution or later order terminated the emergency before 2026-10-14.
